newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open lower after Wall Street sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open lower after Wall Street sell-off.

text.p: Tokyo stocks opened lower on Tuesday after a selloff on Wall Street overnight triggered by comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about potential sales of U.S. Treasuries by Japan, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell 116.71 points or 0.57 percent to 20,319.43 in the first 10 minutes of trade. Its September futures stood 90 points lower at 20,320.
"We're likely to see a correction in Tokyo," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

But investor demand for laggards in the technology sector was strong, which would support the market's downside, brokers said. In New York on Monday, the Dow industrials fell about 192 points or 2.5 percent to 7,604. It was the second-largest single-day point drop ever.
In Chicago, Nikkei 225 futures closed at 20,220, down 190 points from their close in Osaka on Monday.

Hashimoto said in New York on Monday he would like the United States to cooperate in stabilising foreign exchange rates because currency volatility might cause the Japanese government to sell its holdings of U.S. government securities.
